name: Cross Mountain Tower Site
summary: Steel I-S fire tower, built 1934 per register (1935 newspaper says soon to be erected), removed 1962; the mountain now has a private Cold War concrete microwave tower.
design: steel I-S tower (register); 80-foot forest fire tower (1935 Gettysburg Times item)
status_note: Fire tower removed in 1962 per the register; a separate Cold War concrete microwave tower (Cannonball) on the mountain is on private property, and no source describes remains of the fire tower
agency: Pennsylvania department of forests (per the 1935 Gettysburg Times item)

access.note: Applies to the Cannonball concrete tower atop Cross Mountain, on private property and not accessible to the public; no access information for the 1934 fire-tower site

events.note: Register: steel I-S tower built 1934. A March 1935 newspaper item says the tower will soon be erected, so the year is disputed

Gettysburg Times item, March 5, 1935: an 80-foot fire tower on Cross Mountain to be erected by the Pennsylvania department of forests, to provide fire detection for western Washington County, Maryland, and Franklin County
Register: steel I-S tower removed in 1962
Cannonball Cold War concrete microwave tower on Cross Mountain abandoned in 1977; a separate structure from the fire tower
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg
